\section[l'inchiesta]{l'inchiesta — the inquiry, the investigation by journalists or officials}

\label{lesson:IT-C284-inchiesta}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the interview, then the Italian for to interview.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: l'inchiesta}
\textbf{l'inchiesta} — \textquotedblleft{}the inquiry, the investigation by journalists or officials\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Il giornale ha fatto un'inchiesta sugli ospedali.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The newspaper ran an inquiry into the hospitals.}
\end{quote}

Police, judges and journalists all run \emph{inchieste}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{inchiesta} is usually traced to Vulgar Latin \emph{inquaesita} \textquotedblleft{}a thing sought into\textquotedblright{}, from Latin \emph{inquīrere} \textquotedblleft{}to search into\textquotedblright{}, built on \emph{quaerere} \textquotedblleft{}to seek\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{l'inchiesta}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{l'inchiesta}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{l'inchiesta}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for the interview, then the Italian for to interview, then say \emph{l'inchiesta} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does l'inchiesta mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The inquiry, the investigation by journalists or officials\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[il reportage]{il reportage — the report from the spot, the feature story}

\label{lesson:IT-C284-reportage}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for to interview, then the Italian for the inquiry.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: il reportage}
\textbf{il reportage} — \textquotedblleft{}the report from the spot, the feature story\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Ha scritto un reportage sulla vita in montagna.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{She wrote a feature on life in the mountains.}
\end{quote}

Said the French way, with the stress on the end. Plural unchanged: \emph{i reportage}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{reportage} was borrowed from French \emph{reportage} (EtymDB), built on \emph{reporter}, a word that came into French from English.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{il reportage}, once more

\section[la testimonianza]{la testimonianza — the testimony, the eyewitness account}

\label{lesson:IT-C284-testimonianza}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the inquiry, then the Italian for the report from the spot.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la testimonianza}
\textbf{la testimonianza} — \textquotedblleft{}the testimony, the eyewitness account\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
La sua testimonianza è molto importante.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Her testimony is very important.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Rendere testimonianza} — to bear witness.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{testimonianza} is built on \emph{testimoniare} \textquotedblleft{}to bear witness\textquotedblright{} with the ending \emph{-anza}; the root is Latin \emph{testimōnium} \textquotedblleft{}evidence\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{testis} \textquotedblleft{}a witness\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for the inquiry, then the Italian for the report from the spot, then say \emph{la testimonianza} again

\section[testimoniare]{testimoniare — to testify, to bear witness}

\label{lesson:IT-C284-testimoniare}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the report from the spot, then the Italian for the testimony.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: testimoniare}
\textbf{testimoniare} — \textquotedblleft{}to testify, to bear witness\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Due persone hanno testimoniato contro di lui.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Two people testified against him.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Testimoniare a favore di qualcuno} — to testify for someone.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{testimoniare} is built on Latin \emph{testimōnium} \textquotedblleft{}evidence\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{testis} \textquotedblleft{}a witness\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[riferire]{riferire — to report, to pass on (what was said)}

\label{lesson:IT-C284-riferire}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the testimony, then the Italian for to testify.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: riferire}
\textbf{riferire} — \textquotedblleft{}to report, to pass on (what was said)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Ti riferisco quello che ha detto il medico.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I am passing on what the doctor said.}
\end{quote}

Present like \emph{capire}: \emph{riferisco}. \emph{Riferirsi a} — to refer to.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{riferire} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{referre} \textquotedblleft{}to carry back, to report\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), built on \emph{ferre} \textquotedblleft{}to carry\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
